title: Ages and Dispensations
subtitle: Eight dispensations, three ages, and time between the eternities
author: Clarence Larkin
sourceTitle: Rightly Dividing the Word (1921), chart on printed page 6 and chapter II, pages 7–28
editionNote: The modern view follows the 1921 book plate, which numbers eight dispensations, and matches the Clarence Larkin Estate’s Chart #108 preview. The smaller PreservedWords reproduction linked earlier omits the printed 8 and labels period 3 “Post Flood”; both reproductions remain available. Numbering and labels here follow the book plate.
description: Larkin arranges eight dispensations inside three ages and distinguishes the Rapture from the Revelation. His unnumbered judgment interval and the Alpha and Omega eternities are retained separately. The arrangement is a study of his historical interpretation; widths do not measure elapsed time.

periods.title: ALPHA OR “CREATIVE AGES”
periods.summary: The chart places the Alpha or Creative Ages in eternity before its Time envelope. In the accompanying chapter, Larkin describes an original creation and a later restoration before Adam.
periods.sourceExcerpt: This creation was in the dateless past.

details.label: Chart position
details.text: Left of “Time between the Eternities”; unnumbered.

details.label: Interpretive distinction
details.text: Larkin’s original creation / chaotic earth / restoration sequence belongs to his exposition. It is not a ninth numbered dispensation.

periods.sourceLocation: Chart, left eternity field; chapter II §I, “The Creative Ages,” printed pages 9–18.
periods.referenceBasis: Accompanying chapter II, §I; these citations are not printed in the Alpha field.

periods.title: EDENIC DISPENSATION
periods.summary: The Edenic period is the first of the two dispensations in Larkin’s Antediluvian Age. He identifies its governing condition as innocence and leaves its duration unknown.
periods.sourceExcerpt: This Dispensation extends from the creation of Adam to the Expulsion from the Garden.

details.label: Administration
details.text: Innocence, in the accompanying chapter.

details.label: Chart labels
details.text: Eden; The Fall; Paradise Lost.

periods.referenceBasis: Genesis 2:17 is cited in the following paragraph on the transition from innocence to conscience; the Edenic circle itself prints no verse.

periods.title: ANTEDILUVIAN DISPENSATION
periods.summary: Larkin identifies the interval from the Fall to the Flood with conscience. The original circle contrasts the lines of Seth and Cain, and labels its Adam-to-Noah span as 1,656 years.
periods.sourceExcerpt: This extends from the “Fall” to the “Flood.”

periods.referenceBasis: Accompanying chapter II, §II.2; the circle itself prints no verse.

periods.title: POST DILUVIAN
periods.summary: The chart’s third circle runs from Noah to Abraham. Larkin’s chapter describes human government and treats Babel’s divided languages and scattered peoples as its failure.

periods.end: Surrender of the Perfect Kingdom to the Father

events.title: Creation of Adam
events.summary: The Edenic dispensation begins with Adam’s creation in Larkin’s chapter.

events.title: The Fall · Paradise Lost
events.summary: The chart places the Fall at the transition out of Eden, with Paradise Lost below the first circle.

events.title: The Flood
events.summary: The Flood ends the Antediluvian Age and begins the Present Age in this chart.
events.sourceLocation: Chart, boundary between circles 2 and 3; chapter II §II.2–III.

events.title: Babel and the scattering
events.summary: The chapter describes Babel as the failure of human government. The plate’s Noah-to-Abraham interval still retains Abraham as its endpoint.

events.title: Call of Abraham
events.summary: The chart transitions from Noah-to-Abraham to Abraham-to-Moses; the chapter calls the latter’s beginning Abraham’s call.
events.sourceLocation: Chart, circles 3–4; chapter II §III.2, printed page 23.

events.title: The Exodus · Moses
events.summary: The chapter closes the Patriarchal period at the Exodus and begins the Legal period there.

events.title: First Coming
events.summary: The plate compresses the First Coming beside the cross. The chapter separately specifies Christ’s birth as the Legal period’s endpoint.
events.sourceLocation: Chart, First Coming and cross; chapter II §III.3–4, printed page 24.

events.title: Resurrection of Christ · First Fruits
events.summary: The first upward line out of the Grave is labelled Resurrection of Christ and First Fruits.
events.sourceLocation: Chart, lower vertical line beside the cross.

events.title: Ascension
events.summary: The upward line labelled Ascension leads to the Priesthood of Christ above the Church interval.
events.sourceLocation: Chart, upward line above the cross.

events.title: Descent of the Holy Spirit
events.summary: The downward line beside the Ascension marks the Holy Spirit’s descent; the chapter names Pentecost as the believer’s starting point.
events.sourceLocation: Chart, downward line at the Church’s beginning; chapter II §III.4.

events.title: Rapture · First Resurrection · Harvest
events.summary: The Rapture precedes the Tribulation. The rising line from the Grave is labelled First Resurrection and Harvest.
events.sourceLocation: Chart, rising lines at the Church’s right boundary.

events.title: Judgment Seat of Christ
events.summary: The plate places this judgment above the Rapture/Tribulation interval, distinct from the later Great White Throne.
events.sourceLocation: Chart, upper cloud-shaped judgment; chapter II, printed page 25.

events.title: Revelation · Second Coming · Olivet
events.summary: Christ’s second-stage return ends the Present Age and introduces the Age of Ages. It is distinct from the Rapture.
events.sourceLocation: Chart, descending Revelation line and Olivet; chapter II, printed pages 7 and 23.

events.title: Closing rebellion
events.summary: The chapter places Satan’s release and humanity’s final rebellion at the Millennium’s close.

events.title: Renovation of the earth by fire
events.summary: Larkin places this fiery transition between the Millennial and Perfect Ages.
events.sourceLocation: Chart, fire between circles 7 and 8; chapter II, printed pages 27–28.

events.title: Second Resurrection · Tares
events.summary: The last rising line from the Grave bears the labels Second Resurrection and Tares and reaches the Great White Throne.
events.sourceLocation: Chart, right-hand line from the Grave.

events.title: Great White Throne Judgment
events.summary: This judgment is drawn beyond the Millennium at the transition to the Perfect Age, separate from the Judgment Seat of Christ.

events.title: The Kingdom surrendered to the Father
events.summary: In Larkin’s chapter, this surrender closes Time and opens the Omega Ages of the Ages.

parallelBands.title: “Time” between the Eternities
parallelBands.summary: The entire bounded central envelope; Alpha and Omega sit outside it.

parallelBands.title: The Grave
parallelBands.summary: The original lower channel starts at the Fall and continues to the Second Resurrection, with earlier upward branches for Christ’s First Fruits and the Harvest.

parallelBands.title: Times of the Gentiles
parallelBands.summary: A distinct line begins within the Legal period at Larkin’s printed “B.C. 606” and ends at the Revelation. This is not identical to the Fulness of the Gentiles.
parallelBands.sourceLocation: Chart, horizontal line beneath the Present Age.

parallelBands.title: Fulness of the Gentiles
parallelBands.summary: Printed within the Church interval; distinguish it from the longer Times of the Gentiles.
parallelBands.sourceLocation: Chart, lower Church band; chapter II §III.4.

parallelBands.title: Kingdom in Mystery
parallelBands.summary: The original upper band immediately over The Church.

parallelBands.title: Priesthood of Christ
parallelBands.summary: The upper bracket runs from the Ascension to the Judgment Seat of Christ.

parallelBands.title: Kingdom of the Son of Man
parallelBands.summary: Larkin groups both the Millennial and Perfect Ages under this kingdom label.
parallelBands.sourceLocation: Chart, Age of Ages; chapter II §IV.2.

notes.title: Which original is being followed?
notes.text: This study follows the plate on printed page 6 of Larkin’s 1921 Rightly Dividing the Word, cross-checked with the Estate’s Chart #108. The earlier PreservedWords reproduction is retained as an alternate, but is not used to overwrite the book’s printed numbering.

notes.title: Eight numbered dispensations, plus a judgment parenthesis
notes.text: The book chart and chapter II explicitly include an eighth dispensation, Fulness of Times. The Tribulation is unnumbered on the plate; the prose additionally calls it a parenthetical Dispensation of Judgment. Its existence is retained without changing the eight-number sequence.

notes.title: The ages are not interchangeable with the dispensations
notes.text: Larkin distinguishes an age by physical changes in the earth and a dispensation by a moral or probationary administration. Antediluvian Age includes two dispensations; Present Age contains the subsequent four and closes at the Revelation; Age of Ages contains the Millennial and Perfect Ages.

notes.title: Exact Legal and Ecclesiastical endpoints
notes.text: Chapter II ends the Legal Dispensation at Christ’s birth. For the Ecclesiastical Dispensation it specifies Cross-to-Crown for Christ and Pentecost-to-Rapture for the believer. The chart also uses “Christ to Antichrist.” These are preserved as source distinctions, rather than harmonized into a new boundary.

notes.title: Perfect Age is not the outer Omega field
notes.text: Larkin places the Perfect Age/Fulness of Times inside the Age of Ages and Time. He places the subsequent Omega Ages of the Ages outside Time, after the kingdom is surrendered to the Father.

notes.title: Durations remain historical source labels
notes.text: The plate prints 1656 years for Adam-to-Noah, 1491 years for Moses-to-Christ, 1000 years for the Messianic Dispensation, and B.C. 606 on the Gentile-times line. The chapter adds 430 years for Abraham’s-call-to-Exodus and places Babel 325 years after the Flood. These are Larkin’s labels, not independently established chronology or dates for predicting the present.

notes.title: KJV passages and the author’s interpretation
notes.text: Scripture references are taken from the plate or Larkin’s accompanying chapter and identified by location. The KJV reader is separate from Larkin’s historical commentary. The chart’s interpretive framework is attributed to Larkin rather than presented as wording quoted from the Bible.

notes.title: What the modern diagram changes
notes.text: The layout is a schematic reading aid, with modern spacing and navigation. It retains the original period labels, numbering, major relationships and events; it does not claim that column width measures time. The zoomable original preserves every drawn detail.

sourceText:
SELECTED PASSAGES FROM CHAPTER II — AGES AND DISPENSATIONS
Clarence Larkin, Rightly Dividing the Word, 1921.
These selected passages are a reading aid, not the complete chapter. Use the linked original scan to inspect the complete text and its typography. Quotation marks are normalized below; wording is retained.

PRINTED PAGE 18 — EDENIC DISPENSATION
This Dispensation extends from the creation of Adam to the Expulsion from the Garden. As to its duration we know nothing. It was probably very short, and was the “Dispensation of INNOCENCE.”

PRINTED PAGE 18 — ANTE-DILUVIAN DISPENSATION
This extends from the “Fall” to the “Flood.” It was the “Dispensation of CONSCIENCE,” and shows what man will do when guided only by his conscience.

PRINTED PAGE 23 — THE PRESENT AGE
This “Age” extends from the Flood to the second stage of Christ’s Second Coming, called the “Revelation.” It covers four Dispensations.

PRINTED PAGE 23 — POST-DILUVIAN DISPENSATION
This was the “Dispensation of HUMAN GOVERNMENT.”

PRINTED PAGES 23–24 — PATRIARCHAL DISPENSATION
This Dispensation extended from the “Call of Abraham” to the “Exodus,” a period of 430 years, and is known as the “Dispensation of THE FAMILY.”

PRINTED PAGE 24 — LEGAL DISPENSATION
This Dispensation extended from the “Exodus” to the “Birth of Christ,” and is known as the “Dispensation of LAW.”

PRINTED PAGE 24 — ECCLESIASTICAL DISPENSATION
This is the “Dispensation of GRACE,” and extends from the “Cross” to the “Crown” for Christ, and from “Pentecost” to the “Rapture of the Church” for the Believer.

PRINTED PAGE 25 — PARENTHETICAL JUDGMENT
Between the “Ecclesiastical” and “Millennial” Dispensations there is another “Parenthetical Dispensation” the “DISPENSATION OF JUDGMENT,” during which the Jews, the Gentiles, and the Church are to be judged.

PRINTED PAGE 25 — THE AGE OF AGES
This is a “Dual Age,” and includes the “Millennial Age” and the “Perfect Age,” between which the earth is “Renovated by Fire.”

PRINTED PAGE 27 — THE MILLENNIAL AGE
This is not only an “Age,” it is also a “Dispensation,” the “Messianic Dispensation” or rule of Christ as King.

PRINTED PAGE 28 — THE PERFECT AGE
This “Perfect Kingdom” is also a “Dispensation,” the “Dispensation of the FULNESS OF TIMES.” Eph. 1:10. The “Millennial Kingdom” and the “Perfect Kingdom” make up the “Kingdom of the SON OF MAN.”

PRINTED PAGE 28 — THE AGES OF THE AGES
With the surrender of the “Perfect Kingdom” to the Father, what we speak of as “Time” ceases, and the “Eternal Ages,” called the “Ages of the Ages” begin.
